oneliner.t: First-term Republican congressman, Army Reserve intelligence officer and former Maricopa County prosecutor who lost the 2022 attorney-general race by 280 votes and pursued that loss through state courts until December 2024; Trump-endorsed and unopposed in the 2026 primary, he faces Democrat Bernadette Greene-Placentia on Nov. 3.

born.note: Single secondary source (Wikipedia); not confirmed by a second source.

hometown.t: Phoenix area, Arizona (family moved from Chicago; Cactus Shadows High School)

profile.residence: Scottsdale, AZ (residence listed on House disclosure)

upbringing.t: Born in Chicago, the youngest child of Syrian immigrants (a Muslim father and Druze mother), and raised in the Phoenix area; his House biography says his family's first home was near Happy Valley Road and 67th Avenue in what is now the 8th District. He graduated from Cactus Shadows High School, earned a bachelor's degree at Arizona State University and a J.D. at the University of Arizona, interned in the Tucson City Prosecutor's Office, passed the bar in 2016 and joined the Maricopa County Attorney's Office. He describes himself as non-denominational. His brother Waseem Hamadeh, a Phoenix real-estate worker, has been his largest financial backer; the brother's actions are his own.

platform.t: Campaign site lists border, military/veterans, crime, cutting taxes, election integrity and the Second Amendment, framed around Trump's 'America First' agenda; no detailed positions are posted on the homepage.

Has supported Trump's claims that he won 2020 (Wikipedia calls them false); in 2026 alleged fraud in the Los Angeles mayoral election and called for federalizing elections; opposed Arizona's Prop 140 (2024); wants a federal ban on ranked-choice voting.
In 2022 said as attorney general he would enforce Arizona's territorial-era near-total ban; in 2024 said abortion should be left to the states.
Supports finishing the border wall, ending 'catch and release' and designating cartels as terrorist organizations.
Called for repealing and replacing the ACA, opposed Medicaid expansion, and called for no taxes on Social Security; signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.
Strong supporter of Israel; supports sanctions on China and Iran and stopping Ukraine funding; in May 2025 praised Kurdistan Region energy deals and the Peshmerga.

election_contest_2022.court: Mohave County Superior Court, Judge Lee Jantzen (Contest II, filed Dec. 9, 2022 with the RNC and two voters)
election_contest_2022.t: After a trial on alleged election-worker errors, ruled from the bench for Mayes and the other defendants; Hamadeh did not meet his burden of proof.

election_contest_2022.court: Mohave County Superior Court, Judge Jantzen
election_contest_2022.t: Denied his motion for a new trial (based on uncounted Pinal County provisional ballots found in the recount).

Refused his special action to skip the Court of Appeals, ordered Jantzen to issue a signed final ruling, and sanctioned his side for misrepresenting that it had sought a final judgment; fees to Mayes and Fontes (fee order Oct. 17, 2023).

election_contest_2022.court: Arizona Court of Appeals (2–1: Gass, Cattani; Morse dissenting)
election_contest_2022.t: Affirmed denial of a new trial; held provisional ballots cast in the wrong precinct cannot be counted and Pinal votes would not change the outcome.
Rejected his petition for review (filed May 2024).

election_contest_2022.court: Maricopa County Superior Court, Judge Susanna Pineda (quo warranto, filed Dec. 2023)
election_contest_2022.t: Dismissed his bid to remove Mayes; ruled his early-ballot signature theory legally wrong; sanctioned him and attorney Ryan Heath and approved fee requests. Oct. 2024: Court of Appeals affirmed on timeliness but rescinded the fee order.

election_contest_2022.court: Maricopa County Superior Court, Judge Scott Blaney (filed Nov. 2023)
election_contest_2022.t: Dismissed his printer-problem claims as an untimely election contest; declined to award the county fees, finding no sanctionable conduct.

legal.t: The Arizona Supreme Court sanctioned the petitioners in his 2022 election case (reported as Hamadeh, the RNC and/or his legal team) for misrepresenting that they had sought a final judgment, and awarded attorney fees to Mayes and Fontes (order Oct. 17, 2023; Wikipedia gives about $55,000). Sources differ on whether the sanction ran to him personally or to his lawyers.

research_notes: 2022 RESULT: Mayes won by 280 votes after the automatic recount (511 before); certified Dec. 5, 2022; Judge Timothy Thomason announced recount results Dec. 29, 2022. Wikipedia says the Oct. 2023 Supreme Court fee order was about $55,000 — not confirmed by a second source. The Marathon Strategies profile also reports that as a teen he bragged about casting his mother's absentee ballot and that his father overstayed a visa; the first is single-sourced and left out, the second is his father's record, not his. 2024 PRIMARY: Blake Masters' campaign called him a 'terrorist sympathizer'; Trump dual-endorsed both two days before the primary; he won with 29.9%. FAMILY: his brother Waseem funded ABE PAC and his 2022 campaign; that is the brother's spending, reported as funding context only. Primary July 21, 2026: 69,182 votes, unopposed. 2024 general: 56.5% over Gregory Whitten. Photo not retrieved.
